content.transcript: Urban farming can bring food production closer to consumers and make unused spaces productive. Rooftops, balconies, and small community plots can all contribute, but yields are limited by space, sunlight, water, and maintenance. The speaker argues that urban farming is best viewed as a useful supplement to regional agriculture rather than a complete replacement for it.

key_points: it supplements rather than replaces wider agriculture
